SugarCraft\Async

AsyncCache final class

Loop-free async cache-aside primitive (needs no event loop: arms no timers): TTL freshness, concurrent-loader dedupe, optional serve-stale-on-error.

MethodSummary
static new(float $ttlSeconds = 60.0, bool $serveStaleOnError = false, ?callable $clock = null, ?int $maxEntries = null): self
ttlSeconds(): floatFreshness window for cache hits (seconds).
servesStaleOnError(): bool
maxEntries(): ?intThe stored-key cap, or null when unbounded (the default).
generation(): intEpoch of the store: advanced by every invalidate() and clear(). A caller that starts a load records the epoch first and discards the result when the epoch has moved on, the same guard phlix's stores hand-rolled as a generation counter. Shared by every handle over the store.
count(): intNumber of stored values, fresh or stale. In-flight loads are not stored.
keys(): arrayStored keys (fresh or stale), least-recently-stored first.
isLoaded(string $key): boolTrue when the key is fresh OR a load is in flight — the loading-indicator read.
ageSeconds(string $key): ?floatMonotonic age of the stored value, fresh or stale; null when none is held. Reads past the TTL on purpose: stale-serving and age reporting both consult peek semantics, not freshness.
withTtl(float $ttlSeconds): self
withServeStaleOnError(bool $serveStaleOnError): self
withMaxEntries(?int $maxEntries): self
fetch(string $key, callable $loader): PromiseInterfaceCache-aside load: answer from a fresh entry, join the in-flight load, or start one.
peek(string $key): mixedLast stored value for a key, fresh or stale — the render-path read. Null covers both "never loaded" and "loaded as null"; has() tells them apart.
has(string $key): boolTrue when a value (fresh or stale) is held for the key.
isFresh(string $key): boolTrue when a value is held and its TTL has not elapsed.
invalidate(string $key): voidDrop a key and supersede any in-flight load: the next fetch starts fresh, and the displaced arrival resolves its own callers without adopting into the store.
clear(): voidDrop every entry and supersede every in-flight load.

AsyncOps final class

Static helpers for async operations on top of ReactPHP.

MethodSummary
static setLogSink(?callable $sink): voidRedirect (or restore) the destination of swallowed-failure notices.
static withTimeout(PromiseInterface $promise, float $seconds, ?LoopInterface $loop = null, ?string $label = null): PromiseInterfaceWrap a promise with a timeout. If the timeout fires before the promise settles, the returned promise rejects with TimeoutException. The inner promise is NOT cancelled and keeps running to completion. The wait itself is abandonable: cancel() on the returned promise releases the timer and rejects with OperationCancelledException — abandon, not abort (stopping the work is withDeadline()'s contract). When the work itself must stop as the wait ends — a hung I/O holding its consumer's in-flight gate open forever — use withDeadline(), which cancels the inner operation on both expiry and abandonment.
static withDeadline(PromiseInterface $promise, float $seconds, ?LoopInterface $loop = null, ?callable $onTimeout = null, ?string $label = null): PromiseInterfaceWrap a promise with a deadline that CANCELS the inner promise when it fires; withTimeout() by contrast lets the inner run on.
static cancellable(PromiseInterface $promise, ?CancellationToken $token, ?callable $onCancel = null, ?string $label = null): PromiseInterfaceBind a promise to a CancellationToken: cooperative, two-sided, immediate cancellation.
static singleFlight(callable $keyFn, callable $worker): callableCoalesce concurrent invocations of an async worker by key.
static retry(callable $operation, int $attempts = 3, float $baseBackoffSeconds = 0.1, ?CancellationToken $token = null, ?float $maxTotalSeconds = null, float $jitter = 0.0, ?LoopInterface $loop = null, ?callable $now = null, ?callable $onRetry = null): PromiseInterfaceRetry a callable $attempts times in total with exponential backoff.
static all(iterable $promises): PromiseInterfaceFan-in: resolve with every value once ALL promises resolve, preserving keys; reject with the FIRST error the moment one arrives. Non-promise entries are treated as already-resolved values. An empty set resolves with []. These combinators are the package's own promise vocabulary: callers need all() and race() here and never reach past this package for a fan-in primitive.
static race(iterable $promises): PromiseInterfaceFan-in: settle with whichever settles first — value or error. The empty set is a refusal, not a forever-pending promise — that shape renders as a screen frozen with no error to show.
static pendingNotice(PromiseInterface $promise, float $seconds, callable $onPending, ?LoopInterface $loop = null): PromiseInterfaceAnnounce slowness without interrupting the wait. If $promise is still pending after $seconds, $onPending runs ONCE (a "taking longer than expected" spinner hint). The returned promise tracks the inner one — the notice neither cancels nor abandons the work, and the E646 rule holds: this is an advisory tick, never a wall-clock killer of user-paced operations. A hook that throws is logged, never propagated.
static boundWait(PromiseInterface $promise, float $seconds, ?LoopInterface $loop = null, ?string $label = null): PromiseInterfaceBound the wait without stopping the work. If $promise is still pending after $seconds, the returned promise rejects with a TimeoutException whose message names (still pending) — the inner operation keeps running, like under withTimeout(). These are the bounded-wait semantics for user-paced operations: this library puts no blanket wall-clock timeout on operations whose pace belongs to the user. To announce a slow wait instead of ending it, use pendingNotice().
static debounce(callable $fn, float $seconds, ?LoopInterface $loop = null, ?CancellationSource $source = null): DebouncedWrap a callable with debounce — only the last call within the window fires, and only after $seconds have elapsed since it.
static throttle(callable $fn, float $seconds, ?LoopInterface $loop = null, bool $trailing = false): ThrottledWrap a callable with throttle — the function fires at most once every $seconds, regardless of call frequency. Leading-edge by default: calls inside the window answer null. With $trailing true, the LAST suppressed call fires when the window closes instead, and that fire consumes a fresh window — the cap holds at every edge.
static retryBounded(callable $operation, callable $shouldRetry, int $budgetMs, Backoff $backoff, ?callable $now = null, ?callable $sleep = null): mixedSynchronous poll-until-final under a wall-clock budget. Forwards to Retry::bounded() so callers that already import AsyncOps need no second entry point; unlike retry() this blocks and keys off the result (not a rejection).
static nap(int $owedMicros, ?callable $sleeper = null, ?callable $now = null, ?callable $onBeat = null): voidPay a sleep debt that survives signal interruption. Forwards to Retry::nap().
static reconnect(callable $dial, Backoff $backoff, ?CancellationToken $token = null, ?LoopInterface $loop = null, ?callable $onRetry = null): PromiseInterfaceRedial until a connection succeeds or the token fires. Forwards to Retry::reconnect().
static drain(array $pipes, float $deadline, int $maxBytes, ?callable $clock = null, bool $stopAtCap = false, array $discard = [], ?callable $running = null): DrainResultDrain several child pipes against one deadline. Forwards to ChildPump::drain().
static deferred(\Closure $fn, ?LoopInterface $loop = null): PromiseInterfaceRun $fn on the next loop tick instead of inline, answering its result as a promise. Use it to take a slow or re-entrant step off the caller's stack: the caller gets control back now, and $fn runs once the current callback has returned.

Backoff final class

One pure backoff law: exponential ceiling, optional full jitter, and a server-supplied hint that outranks both.

MethodSummary
static new(float $baseMs, float $factor = 2.0, ?int $capMs = null): self
withJitter(?callable $rng = null): selfWait a uniform draw over [0, ceiling] instead of the ceiling itself.
withoutJitter(): selfBack to the deterministic ceiling.
serverHint(?float $seconds): selfThe server's own instruction (seconds, e.g. a parsed Retry-After). While set, forAttempt() returns it un-jittered and un-capped by $capMs — clamping a server's instruction is the caller's policy, applied before it gets here. Null clears it.
withAttempts(?int $attempts): selfTotal tries allowed; null (the default) retries forever. See allows().
allows(int $n): boolWhether a retry may follow the $n-th failure: with N total attempts the N-th failure is final. Always true for the null (forever) budget.
ceiling(int $n): intThe deterministic ceiling after the $n-th failure, ms. 0 for $n < 1.
forAttempt(int $n): intHow long to wait after the $n-th failure, in whole milliseconds: the server hint if one is set, else the ceiling — drawn down by full jitter when enabled.
secondsForAttempt(int $n): floatforAttempt() in seconds.

Cancellable interface

Contract for a component that can be cancelled.

MethodSummary
isCancelled(): boolReturns true if cancel() has been called.
cancel(): voidRequests cancellation. Idempotent — calling multiple times has no additional effect. All registered onCancel callbacks fire in registration order, exactly once.
onCancel(callable $callback): SubscriptionRegister a callback to fire when cancellation is requested. The callback receives no arguments. A throwing callback is logged and never propagated — see CancellationToken::fireCallbacks() for the one hook-failure contract shared across this library. Returns a handle that removes the registration while it is still pending.

CancellationSource final class

Owns the mutable cancellation state and hands consumers the token view; triggering belongs by convention to this source's cancel().

MethodSummary
__construct()
static new(): selfFactory for idiomatic construction.
token(): CancellationTokenReturns the read-only token for this source.
isCancelled(): boolThe state lives in the token (single source of truth): a cancellation raised through the token's internal paths is visible here too, so the source and its token can never disagree on isCancelled().
cancel(): voidRequests cancellation. Idempotent — calling multiple times is a no-op. All callbacks registered on the token fire exactly once, in order. A throwing callback is logged and never propagates from here.
onCancel(callable $callback): SubscriptionRegister a cancellation callback on this source's token. Part of the Cancellable contract — the contract makes it public. Returns the removal handle; see CancellationToken::onCancel().

CancellationToken final class

Read-only view of a cancellation state.

MethodSummary
__construct(CancellationSource $source)
static none(): selfThe shared never-cancelled token.
isCancelled(): boolReturns true if the source has been cancelled.
onCancel(callable $callback): SubscriptionRegister a callback to fire when cancellation is requested. Public contract (mirrors Cancellable::onCancel() — the contract itself makes it public, no visibility games). Fires immediately if the token is already cancelled, otherwise runs at most once, when cancel() happens. Either way a callback that throws is logged, never propagated: the immediate-fire path shares cancel()'s hook-failure seam, so registration cannot surface what cancellation promises to contain.

ChildCapture final class

The per-slot byte ledger shared by the select arm, the Windows poll arm and the loop-driven ChildRun::launch(): keeps the HEAD of each retained slot up to a ceiling, counts what the ceiling refused, and offers every chunk to the live feed before any of that.

MethodSummary

anyFull(): boolWhether any retained slot has reached the ceiling.

ChildPump final class

Read a child's output pipes to EOF without letting one wedge another, bounded by a deadline and a per-stream byte ceiling.

MethodSummary
static new(array $pipes): self
withDeadline(float $deadline): selfAbsolute instant on the clock's scale; default is ten seconds after pump() starts.
withCap(int $maxBytes): selfPer-retained-stream ceiling in bytes (>= 0).
withStopAtCap(bool $stopAtCap = true): selfEnd the walk when a retained stream reaches the cap (the caller kills the child anyway).
withDiscard(array $slots): self
withSlice(float $seconds): selfLongest single select wait before the deadline is rechecked.
withSelectRetries(int $retries): self
withClock(?callable $clock): self
withSelect(?callable $select): selfThe stream_select() seam (POSIX arm); tests inject an EINTR-shaped false.
withRunning(?callable $running): selfWhether the child is still running (WindowsPipes::runningProbe()).
withPollPipes(?bool $pollPipes): selfForce the Windows (true) or select (false) arm; null picks by the real runtime.
withOnChunk(?callable $onChunk): selfLive feed: called with (slot, bytes) for every chunk read, including the slots that are drained but not kept. A TUI tail or a log tee rides this.
withStdin($pipe, string $bytes): selfFeed $bytes to $pipe (the child's stdin) while the walk reads, then close $pipe: the child sees EOF. Refused on the Windows arm (LogicException).
withOnStdinWrite(?callable $onStdinWrite): selfCalled with the byte count of every stdin write the child accepted, as it happens. A child that keeps taking its stdin is alive and working, so a caller with an idle budget counts these writes as activity. Null removes the hook.
withHeartbeat(float $seconds, callable $onBeat): selfCall $onBeat at most every $seconds while the walk is still open. The first beat comes one interval in, not at the start.
withReap(?callable $reap): selfRun $reap once after the walk ends, after the last read, in a finally: the caller reaps the child (or kills it) only once its pipes are drained.
withExitGrace(?float $seconds): selfSelect arm, with a withRunning() probe: once the probe reports the child gone, keep reading until the pipes have been silent for $seconds, then end the walk as CLOSED. The budget counts from the later of the exit and the last chunk read, so a descendant that keeps writing keeps the walk reading (up to the deadline), and one that goes quiet is cut $seconds after its last write. A pipe still open at that cut is reported as abandoned on the result. The Windows poll arm ignores this budget and ends on the fixed WindowsPipes::EXIT_DRAIN_GRACE_SECONDS (see the class docblock).
pump(): DrainResultRead the pipes until they are all at EOF, the deadline passes, or the cap stops the walk, and return what was read and why it stopped.
static drain(array $pipes, float $deadline, int $maxBytes, ?callable $clock = null, bool $stopAtCap = false, array $discard = [], float $sliceSeconds = 0.1, int $selectRetries = self::SELECT_RETRIES, ?callable $select = null, ?callable $running = null, ?bool $pollPipes = null): DrainResultStatic entry kept for the callers that predate the builder (AsyncOps::drain and candy-code's three call sites). Same contract as before the builder: see the class docblock for each argument. New code uses new().

ChildRun final class

Run one child process with a deadline and a per-stream byte cap, and collect what it wrote: blocking with run(), or on a loop with launch().

MethodSummary
static new(array $argv): self
static commandLine(string $line): selfA command line proc_open() takes as one string, so the shell reads it: /bin/sh -c on POSIX, and cmd.exe on Windows. That is the form a shell string had before it was wrapped in an argv. An argv is escaped one element at a time on Windows, and the escaping of an embedded quote is not what cmd.exe reads, so a string command must travel as the raw line. Use new() for any command that is an argv already.
withTimeout(float $seconds): selfSeconds from the start of the run before the child is killed.
withExitGrace(?float $seconds): selfHow long run() and launch() read on after the child's exit is seen, when a backgrounded grandchild still holds the output pipes. The budget is silence: the pipes are read until none has yielded a chunk for this many seconds, then abandoned. The default is the WindowsPipes grace. Null removes the grace: the call then reads until EOF or the deadline, so a held pipe keeps it going to its deadline, where the group is killed and the result is TIMED_OUT. Callers that bound a whole command by its budget pass null.
withIdleTimeout(?float $seconds): selfOpt-in silence budget. The child is killed through the kill ladder once it has neither written to stdout or stderr nor accepted a stdin write for this many seconds, and reported as TIMED_OUT. Any chunk read resets the budget, dropped bytes included, and so does each stdin write the child takes: a child still consuming its input is working, not idle. That stdin count needs a pipe. On the Windows runtime a non-empty withStdin() payload is staged to a file with no pipe behind it, so the child's reads of that file are not counted: a child that reads a staged payload slowly and writes nothing is killed once the budget elapses, while it is still accepting its input. Null (the default) disables it, so a quiet child runs until its deadline. Once the child has exited the budget no longer applies: the exit grace governs its held pipes instead.
withCancellation(?CancellationToken $token): selfCancellation: once $token is cancelled the child is killed through the same ladder as the deadline, reaped, and the result reports CANCELLED. The caller holds the CancellationSource and calls cancel() on it. Null removes it.
withMaxBytes(int $bytes): selfBytes kept per stream (>= 0); output past it is read and counted, not kept.
withStdin(?string $bytes): selfPayload for the child's stdin; null or '' gives the child an immediate EOF.
withCwd(?string $dir): self
withEnv(?array $env): self
withGroupPid(?int $pid): selfThe process group the child leads, for a child started behind a containment wrapper. The caller reads it with \SugarCraft\Core\Util\Proc\BoundedShutdown::groupId() while the child is alive. Each kill rung then signals the whole group, so descendants die with the wrapper. Null keeps the direct-child signal.
withSetsidWrapped(bool $wrapped): selfDeclares that the child was started behind a containment wrapper (a setsid prefix the caller adds to the argv), so the child leads its own process group once it has run. The launch path then falls back to the child's pid as the group id when the group was never read while the child lived, which is the case for a shell that backgrounds a job and exits before the first status poll. An unwrapped child leads no group of its own, so leave this false for it.
withOnChunk(?callable $onChunk): selfLive feed: called with (slot, chunk) for every chunk read from stdout (1) or stderr (2), as it arrives, before the result is assembled. The buffered result is unchanged; the callback only observes. Null removes it.
withOnSpawn(?callable $onSpawn): selfSpawn seam: called once, with the child's pid, right after the child starts and before anything is read or signalled. A child started behind a containment wrapper leads its own process group, so this pid is also the group id a kill rung needs; a runner records it here and passes it to withGroupPid() for the rest of the run, because the group id cannot be measured once the child has been reaped. Null removes the callback.
run(): ChildResultRun the child to completion, blocking the caller, and return what it wrote.
launch(LoopInterface $loop): PromiseInterfaceStart the child on $loop and return a promise of its result. The loop is never blocked: output is read by stream callbacks, the deadline is a timer, and the reap is a short periodic check for the exit. A child still running after its kill budget is reaped by that same check once the kernel releases it, never by a blocking proc_close().

StagedStdin final class

Removal of the temp file a Windows child reads as its stdin (see \SugarCraft\Core\Util\Proc\WindowsPipes::stageStdin()). On Windows a file a live child holds open cannot be unlinked, so a removal attempted before the child is reaped can fail with the payload still on disk. The retry decision lives here, apart from the platform, so every platform can test it.

MethodSummary
static removeAfterExit(LoopInterface $loop, string $path, ?callable $unlink = null, int $attempts = self::EXITED_UNLINK_ATTEMPTS, float $retrySeconds = self::EXITED_UNLINK_RETRY_SECONDS): voidRemoves the payload once the child has been reaped, so the child no longer holds it. A refused removal is retried on the loop a bounded number of times, the first attempt included, and then left behind: the retries never block.
static removeOrRetry(string $path, bool $childReaped, ?callable $unlink = null): boolUnlinks $path. A failure while the child is still alive is retry-worthy: the caller keeps the path and removes it again on the reap path. A failure after the reap is final, because the child no longer holds the file.
static reapHook(?string $path, bool $retry, ?callable $unlink = null): ?\ClosureThe callback a reap runs to remove a payload the live child refused. Null when nothing is owed: no path, or a removal that was already final.

TimeoutException final class

Rejection when a time bound is hit: AsyncOps::withTimeout(), AsyncOps::withDeadline() and AsyncOps::retry()'s exhausted budget. Carries the bound that was set (and the operation's label, when the caller gave one) as structured fields, so a handler can report or branch on the duration without parsing the human-readable message.

MethodSummary
__construct(string $message = '', int $code = 0, ?\Throwable $previous = null, private readonly ?float $seconds = null, private readonly ?string $label = null)The constructor is exempt from signature-compatibility rules in PHP, so the extra structured fields ride after the inherited three (message, code, previous); every existing single-argument construction keeps working unchanged.
seconds(): ?floatThe bound in seconds that was exceeded, or null when unknown.
label(): ?stringThe operation label passed to the wrapper, or null when unlabelled.

Timeouts final class

Timeout and deadline combinators: the caller-side bound (withTimeout()) and the work-side bound that cancels the operation (withDeadline()), plus the shared rejection-message vocabulary both use.

MethodSummary
static withTimeout(PromiseInterface $promise, float $seconds, ?LoopInterface $loop = null, ?string $label = null): PromiseInterfaceWrap a promise with a timeout. If the timeout fires before the promise settles, the returned promise rejects with TimeoutException. The inner promise is NOT cancelled and keeps running to completion. The wait itself is abandonable: cancel() on the returned promise releases the timer and rejects with OperationCancelledException — abandon, not abort (stopping the work is withDeadline()'s contract). When the work itself must stop as the wait ends — a hung I/O holding its consumer's in-flight gate open forever — use withDeadline(), which cancels the inner operation on both expiry and abandonment.
static withDeadline(PromiseInterface $promise, float $seconds, ?LoopInterface $loop = null, ?callable $onTimeout = null, ?string $label = null): PromiseInterfaceWrap a promise with a deadline that CANCELS the inner promise when it fires; withTimeout() by contrast lets the inner run on.
static subject(?string $label): string
static cancellationMessage(?string $label): string
static timeoutMessage(?string $label, float $seconds): string
static deadlineMessage(?string $label, float $seconds): string

WindowsPipes final class

sugar-async's handle on sugar-core's CoreWindowsPipes: non-blocking reads of proc_open pipes on Windows, where PHP's own non-blocking machinery does not apply to them. The measurements and reasoning live on the sugar-core class (the primitive sits there so libraries that do not depend on sugar-async can use it too); ChildPump::drain() reads through it.

MethodSummary
static runtimeNeedsIt(): boolWhether THIS PHP runtime has the blocking-pipe behavior (the real OS).
static available($pipe): intBytes readable from $pipe right now, without blocking.
static readAvailable($pipe, int $max = 8192): stringRead what is already waiting in $pipe, at most $max bytes; never blocks.
static runningProbe($process): \ClosureA "child still running" probe for ChildPump::drain()'s running:.
